text:
harper: Quick sync — product wants a succinct battlecard + bench narrative for the launch blog and webinar. Target comps: cloud-managed endpoints, simple LLM APIs, and DIY infra. Goal: emphasize deterministic cost profiles, tail SLAs, and operational guardrails. Can we iterate something by EOD?

nina: Yep. Suggest output: 1) one-page battlecard with 3 short objection handlers, 2) two landing copy variants (engineer & pm), 3) three email subject lines for A/B. Also a tiny benchmark appendix for the slide notes.

joel: For the bench narrative, let's avoid raw price claims. Focus on mechanics: how batching, KV caching, and fallback routing change cost and tail latency. Add a small methodological blurb.

samir: I ran a quick dev bench (90th pct, 4k tokens) — numbers for slide-notes only:
```
Redwood-dedicated (pinned): 100ms
CloudManaged (anonymized): 210ms
API-Simple: 330ms
DIY-multi: 410ms
```
footnote: demo workload; results vary by model size, sequence length, and quantization.

claire: Battlecard top lines (short bullets):
- "Deterministic inference profiles: engineered batching, prefix caching, and quantization playbooks"
- "Unified runtime: one API across hosted, reserved, and private deployments"
- "Availability-first: routing + automatic fallbacks keep user flows healthy"

harper: Nice. Can we phrase objection handlers more outcome-focused? e.g., instead of "we're cheaper" say: "you avoid surprise spend and reduce engineering toil".

nina: Draft objection handlers: 
1) Cloud-managed: "Fast to prototype, but expensive tail events and limited app-level fallbacks. Redwood gives routing+fallbacks and a predictable tail to protect user experience."
2) LLM APIs: "Great for devs. For production you need rollout controls, KV/prefix caching, and workload-aware batching — all built into our runtime."
3) DIY infra: "Owning infra is powerful but increases ops tax. Redwood Private replicates control with a managed control plane to cut long-term maintenance."

joel: For the landing page, two-line variants:
Variant Eng: "Deterministic inference for shipped AI features. One API, engineered caching, and rollout controls so you meet SLAs."
Variant PM: "Ship reliable AI experiences. Unified runtime and automatic fallbacks protect users when models slow down or fail."

samir: Email subject line candidates: 
A) "Benchmarked: lower production tail latency for inference"
B) "How teams eliminate surprise inference spend"
C) "Keep AI features live when models misbehave"

claire: For slides, use anonymized bars and a simple methodology callout: "Dev-run, 90th-pct on 4k tokens, single-region; not representative of all workloads." Also add a tiny diagram: request -> routing -> cache -> model pools -> fallback.

harper: Inbound routing suggestion: tag = "launch-inference-bench". Workflow: immediate email with one-pager + bench highlights; 48h follow-up with 90s demo clip showing canary->fallback; SDR outreach if sample tokens or ARR flags present. Add checkbox: regulated industry -> Private brief.

ops-bot: calendar-bot: tentatively reserved Wed next week 10:00 PT for webinar demo rehearsal. Zoom webinar available.

nina: Demo plan (30s per segment):
- Segment 1: cost math — show estimator mapping a real token mix to monthly spend (anonymized)
- Segment 2: rollout — canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% with metrics visible
- Segment 3: fault injection — simulate slow model, show auto-fallback to variant and no user disruption

joel: Quick visual for slide: two mini-bars (90th, 99th) per vendor + a tiny cost-row per 1M tokens (anonymized numbers). Keep axis labeled and method footnote. No competitor logos.

harper: Timeline:
- By 3pm today: nina battlecard + objection handlers; samir bench artifact; joel slide copy
- By tomorrow 10am: claire landing copy variants + email subjects; ops-bot confirm webinar rehearsal slot
- Tomorrow 4pm: final review and consolidate assets into /marketing/webinar/prelaunch/

claire: One more editorial: avoid framing as price-first; lead with availability and predictable cost profile. Save language about "cheaper" for internal notes only.

samir: Agreed. Also I'll include a tiny CLI snippet in the benchmark appendix showing the exact command used and the model config so customers can reproduce.

harper: Great. nina, ping this thread when draft is up and I'll review. Thanks team :rocket:
